copyright: Black Forest, Baden-Württemberg, Germany (© Britus/Getty Images)
description: The Black Forest in south-west Germany is known for its misty landscapes, forested hills, deep valleys, lakes and picturesque towns. Stretching about 160 kilometres, the region is home to Feldberg, its highest peak at 1,493 metres, and marks the source of both the Danube and Neckar rivers. Beyond its natural beauty, the Black Forest is rich in history and tradition. Forestry has shaped the region for centuries, while its renowned clockmaking heritage helped make the cuckoo clock famous around the world. Today, the area remains one of Germany's most distinctive destinations, blending cultural heritage with striking scenery.

copyright: St. Bartholomew's Cathedral in Frankfurt, Germany (© AlxeyPnferov/Getty Images)
description: Frankfurt, Germany, provides a fitting backdrop for Halloween with St. Bartholomew's Cathedral and its striking Gothic tower. Yet the holiday's origins are even more intriguing. Many Halloween traditions are linked to Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival marking the end of the harvest season and the start of winter. People believed the boundary between the living and the dead grew thin, prompting bonfires, offerings and disguises to ward off wandering spirits. Later, the Christian observances of All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day helped shape Halloween as we know it today. St. Bartholomew's may set the scene, but Halloween brings the ghosts, legends and mystery.

copyright: Sandhill cranes, Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge, New Mexico, USA (© Terry St.Louis/Getty Images)
description: Winter transforms Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge in New Mexico into a haven for wildlife. Established in 1939, the 57,331-acre sanctuary provides an important stopover for migrating waterfowl and supports wildlife year-round. Sandhill cranes, featured in today's image, arrive in late October and spend the winter here, roosting in shallow water at night and feeding in nearby fields at sunrise. The refuge is a key wintering ground for the Rocky Mountain population of sandhill cranes. Other seasonal visitors include snow geese, northern pintails, hawks and eagles, while mule deer, coyotes and other mammals inhabit its diverse habitats.

copyright: Standing stones at Avebury in Wiltshire, England (© George W Johnson/Getty Images)
description: As morning mist drifts among the standing stones of Avebury in Wiltshire, England, the scene feels almost timeless. These ancient megaliths form part of one of the world's most remarkable prehistoric landscapes, centred on a vast Neolithic monument built around 4,500 years ago. Avebury contains the world's largest prehistoric stone circle, as well as a massive henge and stone avenues extending into the surrounding countryside. Together with nearby monuments such as Silbury Hill and West Kennet Avenue, it forms part of an extensive Neolithic complex that has fascinated generations of visitors, researchers and archaeologists.

copyright: Kunětická hora Castle, Bohemia, Czechia (© Marek Saroch/Alamy)
description: What stories could these walls tell? Rising above eastern Bohemia in Czechia, Kunětická hora Castle has witnessed centuries of history. Dating to the late 14th century, the castle gradually evolved into an impressive fortress and noble residence. Its elevated position offered commanding views of the surrounding countryside and helped make it an important stronghold.

copyright: A grove of pond cypress trees with fall foliage, Georgia, United States (© Chris Moore/Getty Images)
description: Reflected in calm water and glowing in the light of the setting sun, this grove of pond cypress creates a striking display of colour and symmetry. Native to the southeastern United States, the species is associated with shallow ponds, depressions and wetland habitats. This image was captured in Georgia, where these trees can be found in places such as the Okefenokee Swamp and other low-lying wetlands.

copyright: Autumn waterfalls near Sitovo, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria (© Nadya85/Getty Images)
description: In Bulgaria's Western Rhodope Mountains, autumn leaves gather beside the rushing waters of Sitovo Waterfall. Near the village of Sitovo, southwest of Plovdiv, the falls tumble beneath an old stone bridge whose arch frames the cascades like a storybook scene. Moss-covered stones and pine trees add shades of green to the autumn landscape, while fallen leaves gather along the water's edge or drift through its pools. The falls become especially lively after rain and during spring snowmelt, when the surrounding woodland echoes with the sound of rushing water.
